summary: The Network-M2 and Network-M3 cards have a user name and password login page, but no public source shows its markup, so there is nothing to write selectors from. The profile stays manual.

sources.title: The existing Eaton profile (the entry with id eaton-ups): manual, no universal login selectors assumed
Public scanner check for the card's web sign-in: a JSON request to the card's own REST service, not a form post
sources.note: Read for the request shape only: the user name and password travel as JSON to /rest/mbdetnrs/1.0/oauth2/token. That says nothing about the page's field ids or names.

staysInteractive.note: The whole sign-in, until a layout is known. According to a search summary of Eaton's user's guides, the first sign-in forces a change of the default password and directory users sign in with a prefix (ldap or radius, then the account).

lookedFor: Eaton's Network-M2 and Network-M3 user's guides on eaton.com: found by search, but two PDF reads timed out, so they were not read. The search summary describes a login page, a forced password change at first sign-in and LDAP and RADIUS accounts. Whether the guides show any markup could not be checked.

Public repositories (searches for the card's REST namespace and for Eaton UPS tools): exporters and home-automation integrations that use the REST service, MQTT or SNMP. None drives or reproduces the login page.
The card's sign-in request, from a public scanner check: JSON to the REST service. That points to a script-rendered page, and the request does not reveal its fields.
Not done: no device was contacted, no firmware was opened, and the capture tool was not run (the profile has no hosted login URL).
neededFromUser: The login page of your card saved as "Webpage, Complete" once it has finished loading, with the card model (Network-M2 or Network-M3) and firmware version. Say also whether you sign in with a local, LDAP or RADIUS account. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: Older Eaton cards (Network-MS and earlier) and Eaton PDUs have other web interfaces and were not researched. If the login is a script-rendered page, as the sign-in request suggests, a saved copy must be the rendered page, not the page source.
